Article Title: 'Rubbing salt into wounds': BJP targets Rahul over Nov 1 rally, recalls 1984 anti-Sikh riots
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: The Bharatiya Janata Party on Saturday upped the ante against Lok Sabha leader of opposition Rahul Gandhi, accusing him of rubbing salt into the wounds of the Sikh community by holding an INDIA bloc rally at Ramlila Maidan on November 1 - the anniversary of the 1984 anti-Sikh riots in Delhi following the assassination of former Prime Minister Indira Gandhi.Addressing a press conference, senior BJP leader Ravi Shankar Prasad questioned the Congress leader's insistence on holding the rally on the date."Why is Rahul Gandhi so adamant about holding his rally in Delhi on November 1? This issue is being raised very seriously by our party. November 1 is a day that holds deep emotional significance for the Sikh community, as they remember the 1984 massacre with profound sorrow," Prasad said."So, by creating a storm at Ramlila Maidan on November 1, what kind of salt does Rahul Gandhi want to rub into their wounds?" he asked.The BJP leader also said that many members of the opposition alliance were not satisfied with the decision to hold the rally on November 1."We have heard that many members of their alliance were also not satisfied with this decision. We have also received information that a virtual meeting was convened on October 22 to discuss this issue.However, since many allies did not attend, the meeting was postponed," he said."We have also learnt that several allies were unhappy with the November 1 date and had suggested that the rally be postponed to a later date. This reflects Rahul Gandhi's true face. When he insists on something, he refuses to listen to anyone. If he is determined to have his way, he will go ahead, even if it means cruelly mocking the sentiments of the Sikh community," the BJP leader said.The opposition rally aims to ramp up pressure on the government over the "vote chori" issue and demand Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar's resignation over alleged irregularities in the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.On October 12, protests over the "vote theft" charge reached the Supreme Court's doorstep, with opposition leaders, activists and civil society members participating in a 'March for Democracy' along a heavily barricaded route in Delhi and filing a joint petition against the SIR.Rahul hosted INDIA bloc leaders for tea at his home on October 13. After the meeting, the opposition bloc vowed to continue resisting and take the "vote chori" fight to its logical conclusion.
Article Summary: Bharatiya Janata Party accuses Rahul Gandhi of rubbing salt into the wounds of the Sikh community by holding an INDIA bloc rally at Ramlila Maidan on November 1. November 1 is the anniversary of the 1984 anti-Sikh riots in Delhi following the assassination of former Prime Minister Indira Gandhi.

Article Title: When Sonia met Rajiv: Congress leader narrates her 1st meeting with husband in X debut
Article Text:
Sonia Gandhi makes X debut, recalls first meeting with Rajiv Gandhi ahead of book launch

Sonia Gandhi recalls meeting Rajiv Gandhi in Cambridge

Upcoming memoir traces her personal journey

NEW DELHI: Congress Parliamentary Party chairperson Sonia Gandhi made her debut on social media platform X on Saturday, sharing a video in which she recalled her first meeting with former Prime Minister Rajiv Gandhi and offered a glimpse of her upcoming book, Belonging: A Journey of Love.The book, Sonia Gandhi's first, is scheduled to be launched on November 10. It recounts her personal journey, including her memories with Rajiv Gandhi and experiences from her younger days to the present.In the nearly two-minute video accompanying her first post on X, Sonia Gandhi recalled meeting Rajiv Gandhi at the Varsity Restaurant, a Greek eatery in Cambridge, England, where they were students.The video featured photographs of the couple and the restaurant where they first met."In a small Greek restaurant in Cambridge, my journey of love began. Rajiv and I created a world filled with love, laughter and memories. On 10th November, I share that world with you," she wrote in her post.Speaking in the video, the Congress MP recalled looking for Italian food while living in England, where she said the food available at the time did not suit her preferences."Food in England in those days was awful. In those days, you didn't have so many restaurants, you know, like you have today," she said.She explained that she was looking for a place serving food closer to what she was accustomed to, particularly Italian cuisine, when she discovered the Greek restaurant."And then, we discovered this place (Varsity Restaurant). It was a Greek restaurant where many European students, but also Indian students, used to go for their meals. And that is then where I met Rajiv in that very restaurant," she said.Recalling her first impression of Rajiv Gandhi, she said she felt almost immediately that he was someone she would want to spend her life with."When I first met him, I felt almost immediately that you know he was someone I would really love to be with. And, of course, I learned that it was the same for him," she said.Sonia Gandhi also recalled that a common friend introduced them. The two subsequently became friends and began attending parties with other students and visiting places together."I remember when I first met him, a friend, a common friend, introduced us. Then, you know, we became friends. Then going to parties with friends, or going to see sights, or… We went to a Valentine party where there were lots of students," she said.Describing what stood out to her about Rajiv Gandhi, she said his gentle nature had left a lasting impression."He was a very gentle-looking person. Of course, he was very good-looking. But that gentleness came through. So that was something which really touched me and struck me. So that, of course, I'll never forget when I first met him," she said.Sonia married Rajiv Gandhi on February 25, 1968.The upcoming memoir, Belonging: A Journey of Love, explores Sonia Gandhi's life, from her childhood in post-war Italy and her romance with Rajiv Gandhi to her move to India and the personal losses that shaped her life and relationship with her adopted country.Her debut on X comes two days after she joined Instagram on Thursday and shared a video offering a first look at the book.In her first Instagram post, she expressed gratitude at being able to share the preview with readers and described the memoir as a story of love, duty, loss and finding a place to belong."I look forward to sharing it with you," she wrote in the post.
Article Summary: Sonia Gandhi makes her debut on social media platform X on Saturday. She shared a video in which she recalled her first meeting with Rajiv Gandhi. She also offered a glimpse of her upcoming book, Belonging: A Journey of Love. The book, Sonia Gandhi's first, is scheduled to be launched on November 10.

Article Title: 'Will not sign': AISA chief Neha Bora defies Delhi police peace bond notice after HC setback
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: All India Students' Association president Neha Bora on Saturday said she would not sign a bond to "keep peace" before a special executive magistrate, a day after the Delhi high court dismissed her plea challenging the police notice directing her to furnish a Rs 10,000 bond with a surety."We don't have any conditions. We are not going to sign the bond," Bora said.Bora had moved the high court, arguing that the notice was vague, factually incorrect and unsupported by material establishing the likelihood of a breach of peace.She alleged that the proceedings were a "colourable exercise of preventive powers to suppress peaceful dissent, in violation of Articles 19(1)(a), 19(1)(b) and 21 of Constitution".During Thursday's hearing, Bora's counsel argued that citizens did not need permission to hoist the national flag, referring to the police notice alleging that she had hoisted it without valid permission.The notice, issued on October 17 under Section 126 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS), directed Bora to appear before the magistrate on October 19 and explain why she should not execute a personal bond of Rs 10,000 with one surety "for keeping peace for a period of enquiry".Bora was taken into preventive detention on October 16 while on her way to participate in the Cockroach Janata Party's (CJP) 'Lehra Do Tiranga' march at Central Park in Connaught Place. She was released the following day.According to her petition, the police initiated proceedings over alleged sloganeering at Mandi House on October 16, repeated protests around Jantar Mantar despite prohibitory orders under Section 163 of the BNSS, and allegations that she had instigated people to join a demonstration at Connaught Place that day."The impugned notice rests on a prima facie incorrect fact, namely that the petitioner instigated people to participate in the demonstration at Central Park, CP on Oct 16. The petitioner's call and the incident alleged were different. The petitioner called for a peaceful gathering at Mandi House at 5.00 pm on Oct 16, and it is a matter of record that she was detained from Mandi House," Bora's petition stated.
Article Summary: All India Students' Association president Neha Bora says she will not sign a bond to "keep peace" before a special executive magistrate. Delhi high court dismissed her plea challenging the police notice directing her to furnish a Rs 10,000 bond with a surety. Bora had moved the high court, arguing that the notice was vague, factually incorrect and unsupported by material establishing the likelihood of a breach of peace.

NEW DELHI: Jammu and Kashmir chief minister Omar Abdullah on Saturday said the expansion and reshuffle of his cabinet would take place in the first two to three days of next week.Talking to reporters, the J&K chief minister said he had met lieutenant governor Manoj Sinha and sought time for the exercise."Yes, it (reshuffle) certainly was (discussed). NEW DELHI: The Chamber of Trade and Industry on Saturday urged Lok Sabha leader of opposition Rahul Gandhi to postpone the INDIA bloc's upcoming rally on November 1 at Ramlila Maidan, saying the demonstration could disrupt business worth Rs 10,000 crore during the peak Diwali shopping season.In a letter to Rahul, CTI chairman Brijesh Goyal said the rally could affect wholesale and retail markets around Ramlila Maidan at a time when traders expect heavy customer footfall ahead of Dhanteras and Diwali."This year, Dhanteras falls on Friday, November 6, Diwali on November 8 and Bhai Dooj on November 10. People begin shopping for Dhanteras and Diwali a week in advance. In Delhi alone, Dhanteras-related business across sectors such as gold and silver, utensils, electronics, textiles, dry fruits, sweets, automobiles, vehicles, property and gift items amounts to approximately Rs 25,000 crore. This trade is the backbone of Delhi's economy," the letter reads.The traders' body said markets generally see increased activity about a week before the festivals, making the timing of the rally a matter of concern.Goyal also said traders in Delhi had already suffered losses of around Rs 3,000 crore in October due to rallies, marches and road closures in Connaught Place, India Gate and central Delhi."According to CTI's estimates, traders in Delhi have already suffered losses of approximately Rs 3,000 crore due to repeated rallies, marches and road closures in Connaught Place, India Gate and central Delhi," he said."The movement of goods into wholesale markets had come to a halt, while retail customers were unable to reach the markets," he added.The organisation also pointed to around 20 wholesale and retail markets within a five-kilometre radius of Ramlila Maidan, including Chandni Chowk, Sadar Bazar, Chawri Bazar, Bhagirath Palace, Khari Baoli, Kashmere Gate, Nai Sarak, Mori Gate, Kinari Bazar, Dariba, Daryaganj, Ajmeri Gate, Jama Masjid, Karol Bagh and Azad Market."Goods from these markets are supplied across the country. Traffic diversions, metro station closures and barricading during the rally could bring business in these markets to a complete standstill," Goyal said.While acknowledging the right to peaceful protest and democratic expression, CTI urged political parties to avoid holding large rallies in key commercial areas until the festival period ends.The opposition rally aims to ramp up pressure on the government over the "vote chori" issue and demand Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar's resignation over alleged irregularities in the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.On October 12, protests over the "vote theft" charge reached the Supreme Court's doorstep, with opposition leaders, activists and civil society members participating in a 'March for Democracy' along a heavily barricaded route in Delhi and filing a joint petition against the SIR.Rahul hosted INDIA bloc leaders for tea at his home on October 13. NEW DELHI: An FIR has been registered against unidentified persons after two posters questioning the government's performance were found pasted inside a train on the Delhi Metro's Airport Express Line, news agency PTI reported citing police sources.The posters, printed in black and white on A4-sized sheets, featured phrases such as "Voting Protest", "You Can Change Your Own Life", "Spectrum of Engagement", "Community Building Reform" and "Dissatisfied? You Are Not Alone".They also listed nine claims about changes in the country in recent years and carried a QR code inviting people to join an online group, the sources said.According to the FIR, the incident came to light on October 20 when Tarun Chaudhary, a Delhi Metro Rail Corporation (DMRC) train operator deployed on the Airport Express Line, spotted the posters during an inspection.Chaudhary had operated a train from New Delhi station to Yashobhoomi, leaving at around 6.50pm and arriving at approximately 7.15pm. While checking the train from inside the cabin, he noticed the two posters pasted on a seat.He removed the material and alerted his senior officers and the Operations Control Centre. He was subsequently instructed to hand the posters over to the station controller at Dwarka Sector 21, who informed the police.The posters were seized by police on Friday, and the special cell has also joined the investigation.
Article Summary: Two posters questioning the government's performance were found inside a train on the Delhi Metro's Airport Express Line. An FIR has been registered against unidentified persons. The posters featured phrases such as "Voting Protest" and "Dissatisfied? You Are Not Alone"

NEW DELHI: Kerala governor Om Prakash Mathur's reported decision to make the Lok Bhavan kitchen vegetarian-only has sparked a political controversy, with Congress leader K C Venugopal accusing him of pushing the Sangh Parivar's agenda.Mathur, the former Sikkim governor, directed that non-vegetarian food should not be prepared or served in the Lok Bhavan kitchen. The reports surfaced on Thursday, a day before he assumed office, news agency PTI reported.Reacting to the reports shortly after Mathur was sworn in as the 29th governor of Keralam, AICC general secretary Venugopal alleged that the decision went beyond the governor's personal food preferences and infringed on individual freedom.Keralam has a diverse food culture and abundant fish resources as a coastal state, Venugopal said, adding that people had the freedom to choose between vegetarian and non-vegetarian food."Any attempt to restrict the food habits Keralites are accustomed to or dictate what they should eat from now on cannot be accepted," he said as quoted by PTI.Venugopal argued that restrictions that "intrude" into people's food choices and seek to erase Keralam's traditional way of life violate fundamental rights guaranteed by the Constitution.He alleged that the governor was using his authority to "curtail" individual freedom instead of protecting people's right to decide what to eat and how to live."This is a continuation of the unconstitutional interests of the Sangh Parivar. This is the first step towards implementing the saffron agenda of the Sangh Parivar in Keralam," the Alappuzha MP alleged.While acknowledging Mathur's right to follow a vegetarian diet, Venugopal said the governor should not impose his personal preferences on the Lok Bhavan kitchen, whose employees include Keralites. He urged Mathur to withdraw any decision restricting food choices.Sources in the governor's office said Mathur was a strict vegetarian and had directed that non-vegetarian food not be prepared in the kitchen where his meals were cooked.They clarified that the kitchen's food was served only to the governor and a few members of his personal staff. Other employees either brought food from home or ate outside, and no restrictions had been imposed on their food choices, the sources said as cited by PTI.They added that fish and meat dishes had been prepared in the Lok Bhavan kitchen during the tenure of some previous governors.
Article Summary: Kerala Governor Om Prakash Mathur’s reported decision to make the Lok Bhavan kitchen vegetarian-only sparks a row. Congress leader K C Venugopal accuses him of pushing the Sangh Parivar's agenda. Sources in the governor's office said Mathur was a strict vegetarian.

Article Title: After Operation Sindoor friction, Delhi & Baku reset ties with EAM Jaishankar's visit
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: Amid ongoing efforts by both India and Azerbaijan for a reset in ties, EAM S Jaishankar and his counterpart Jeyhun Bayramov agreed to expand cooperation in energy, trade, investment and connectivity in a “very productive” meeting in Baku.Jaishankar’s visit to Azerbaijan was the first by an Indian foreign minister in eight years and built upon the diplomatic goodwill created by PM Modi’s meeting with Azerbaijan President Ilham Aliyev on the margins of the SCO summit in Bishkek last month.Ties between the two countries had been held back by geopolitical reasons for a while, mainly Azerbaijan’s ties with Pakistan — as evident from its support for Islamabad after Op Sindoor last year — and India’s defence ties with Armenia.While Bayramov spoke about taking the relationship to a higher level, setting aside past differences, Jaishankar underlined the significance of trade and energy cooperation. Terrorism was also among the issues discussed. “We spoke about economic cooperation, including trade, investment and energy, which are central to our bilateral ties... We believe there is very good scope for further enhancement of bilateral trade and investment.We also discussed various activities and exchanges,” said Jaishankar.“We spoke about connectivity because it is so important in a globalised economy,” he said, adding that they agreed to coordinate more closely on the International North-South Transport Corridor (INSTC).The EAM also called on Aliyev in Baku. “Discussed strengthening relationship between our two countries. Appreciate his positive sentiments for this shared endeavour,” he said.Jaishankar welcomed peace agreement between Azerbaijan and Armenia, expressing hope that it would lead to the establishment of a durable peace.
Article Summary: Jaishankar’s visit to Azerbaijan was the first by an Indian foreign minister in eight years. Ties between the two countries had been held back by geopolitical reasons for a while. Terrorism was also among the issues discussed in a ‘very productive’ meeting.

Article Title: ITBP Raising Day: PM Modi praises ‘Himveers’ as India-China border management remains in focus
Article Text:

Rajnath Singh, Kiren Rijiju salute ITBP personnel

Indian Army extends wishes on ITBP's 65th Raising Day

NEW DELHI: Prime Minister Narendra Modi , Union home minister Amit Shah, defence minister Rajnath Singh and parliamentary affairs minister Kiren Rijiju extended greetings to personnel of the Indo-Tibetan Border Police (ITBP) on the force's Raising Day on Saturday, praising their courage, sacrifices and service in protecting India's borders.The Indian Army also conveyed its wishes to ITBP personnel, veterans and their families on the occasion of the force's 65th Raising Day.In a post on X, Prime Minister Modi praised the force's personnel, known as Himveers, for their valour and determination in facing challenges.“On their Raising Day, greetings to all personnel of the ITBP. The ITBP Himveers have distinguished themselves through their exceptional valour. They have always risen to every challenge with remarkable determination. Their selfless service and sacrifices are a source of immense inspiration to the nation,” PM Modi wrote.Union home minister Amit Shah also extended Raising Day greetings to ITBP personnel, praising their courage in safeguarding the country's security and remembering those who laid down their lives in service to the nation.“The roar of their valour echoes through the snow-clad mountains, reducing every threat to our nation's security to rubble.Their tenacity in withstanding the harshest climates symbolizes India's steely resolve for security. Salutations to the martyrs who made the supreme sacrifice for the nation,” Shah wrote on X.Defence minister Rajnath Singh extended his greetings to ITBP personnel and their families, highlighting their contribution to border security and internal security operations.“On ITBP Raising Day, I extend my warm greetings to all ITBP personnel and their families. The Himveers of ITBP have played a vital role in safeguarding India’s borders in the harshest climatic conditions. They have also made significant contributions to internal security operations, including efforts to combat Left Wing Extremism,” Singh said.He added that their courage, professionalism and commitment to duty reflected the finest traditions of service to the nation.Kiren Rijiju also greeted the Himveers, invoking the force's motto, “शौर्य-दृढ़ता-कर्मनिष्ठा” (valour, steadfastness and devotion to duty).“On the occasion of ITBP Raising Day, I extend my heartfelt greetings to the Himveers of @ITBP_official. Your vital resilience in protecting our borders in extreme conditions is an inspiration. Salute to your spirit of sacrifices & patriotism,” Rijiju wrote on X.The Indian Army also conveyed its greetings to the force. In a post on X, it said General Dhiraj Seth, Chief of Army Staff, and all ranks of the Army extended their “warm greetings and best wishes” to ITBP personnel, veterans and their families on the occasion of its 65th Raising Day.The ITBP is responsible for guarding India's borders with China in challenging high-altitude and climatic conditions.The greetings come amid continuing attention to the situation along the Line of Actual Control (LAC). The ministry of external affairs (MEA) said on Friday that the situation along the India-China border gets disturbed from time to time when Chinese forces diverge from established patrolling patterns.“Both sides continue to use existing diplomatic and military mechanisms to resolve outstanding issues and avoid misunderstanding and miscalculation along the Line of Actual Control (LAC),” MEA spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal said.Jaiswal also said the two countries had agreed to discuss ways to improve their understanding of the LAC in appropriate areas to strengthen border management. He stressed that maintaining peace and tranquillity in border areas was essential for the overall development of bilateral relations.ITBP director general Shatrujeet Kapur had recently spoken about continuing confrontations with Chinese troops at several locations along the border in Arunachal Pradesh.He also said the force had raised drone platoons in all its border units and developed a new 'Strike' course to better handle battles similar to the 2020 Galwan Valley clash.
Article Summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi, Union home minister Amit Shah, defence minister Rajnath Singh and parliamentary affairs minister Kiren Rijiju extended greetings to personnel of the Indo-Tibetan Border Police. The Indian Army also conveyed its wishes to ITBP personnel, veterans and their families on the occasion of the force's Raising Day.

Article Title: Govt plans colour-coded driving licence for Indians, foreigners
Article Text:
Under the draft, the ministry has listed separate sets of documents for proof of address, age and identity. (Generative image)

Govt plans colour-coded DLs for Indians, foreigners

Poll Vote & Share your view Which proposed change do you believe is the most beneficial? NEW DELHI: In a first, govt has proposed mentioning the nationality of driving licence holders on DLs and introducing separate colour schemes for Indian andforeign nationals as well as doing away with affidavits sworn before an executive magistrate or notary as proof of age and address, which has the potential of being misused.Life insurance policies, too, would no longer be accepted as proof. Proposing sweeping changes to the driving licence (DL) regime under Motor Vehicles Rules, the road transport ministry Wednesday issued a draft notification to raise the pass mark for the online safe-driving tutorial assessment from the current 60% to 75%.It has also proposed making it mandatory for licences to carry the holder’s blood group, mobile number and emergency contact details. The ministry has proposed waiving fees for specified DL services, including changes to address, name and contact number, if applicants avail themselves of these services through online Aadhaar authentication.At present, if an applicant cannot produce any of the 12 listed documents, the licencing authority “may accept an affidavit sworn before an executive magistrate, judicial magistrate or notary public as proof of age and address”.Anil Chhikara, an expert in motor vehicle licencing, said, “The use of simple affidavits is being phased out after miscreants used them to register false addresses and dates of birth. Applicants must now provide verifiable documents. ”Under the draft, the ministry has listed separate sets of documents for proof of address, age and identity. Address proofs include Aadhaar card, Electoral Photo Identity Card, e-ration card, electricity or gas bills for the preceding three months, and proof of legal presence for foreign nationals. Acceptable age proofs include passports, school board mark sheets, birth certificates and identity cards issued by govt departments. Aadhaar, passports, e-ration cards and PAN have been listed as acceptable identity proofs.The proposed changes aim to curb the submission of false documents, tighten assessment requirements and make licence-related services more accessible. They also seek to streamline online DL services and set timelines for processing applications to change licence particulars.Under the proposal, the safe-driving tutorial would have to last at least 30 minutes, while the higher qualifying score of 75% is intended to make the assessment more stringent. Licencing authorities would have to approve or reject online applications to change DL particulars, including name and address, within 15 days, giving reasons for rejection.An application for a change of address that remains undecided for 30 days would be deemed approved. The draft also proposes a consolidated application form for services such as DL renewal, issuance of duplicate licences, addition of a vehicle class and changes to personal particulars. Specified applicant details would be retrieved electronically from the Sarathi portal wherever available.
Article Summary: Govt plans colour-coded DLs for Indians, foreigners. Life insurance policies, too, would no longer be accepted as proof. Proposed changes aim to curb the submission of false documents. They also seek to streamline online DL services and set timelines for processing applications.

Article Title: Bihar MLC polls: 5.32 lakh voters to decide fate of 150 candidates across 8 seats, JD(U) rift adds intrigue
Article Text:
Polling began at 8 am today for eight seats in the Bihar Legislative Council (Representative image)





PATNA: Polling for biennial elections to eight Bihar Legislative Council seats began at 8 am on Friday amid tight security, with 5.32 lakh voters eligible to decide the fate of 150 candidates, officials said.Voting will continue till 4 pm for four Graduates and four Teachers constituencies, they said.The combined electorate stands at 5,32,847, including 1,46,611 women and 37 third-gender voters, across 933 polling stations. Counting of votes will take place on October 27.The contest in the Patna Graduates constituency has drawn attention following an open rift within the JD(U), with Mokama MLA Anant Singh backing Jan Suraaj Party candidate Anuj Singh against his own party's nominee, Neeraj Kumar.Kumar, a former minister and a close aide of former chief minister Nitish Kumar, is seeking a fourth consecutive term from the seat.Anant Singh has extended support to Anuj Singh, alleging that Neeraj Kumar had worked against him during last year's assembly elections.Apart from Patna Graduates, the other constituencies going to polls are Darbhanga Graduates, Tirhut Graduates, Kosi Graduates, Patna Teachers, Darbhanga Teachers, Tirhut Teachers and Saran Teachers.The terms of the sitting MLCs are due to expire on November 16.The BJP has fielded candidates in four constituencies, including three sitting MLCs seeking re-election, while the JD(U) has nominated candidates for the remaining four seats.The BJP nominees are MLCs Nawal Kishor Yadav, NK Yadav and Sarvesh Kumar, who are seeking re-election from Patna Teachers, Kosi Graduates and Tirhut Graduates, respectively.The party has also fielded Narendra Kumar Singh from Tirhut Teachers, a seat currently held by Sanjay Kumar Singh of the CPI, a constituent of the opposition INDIA bloc.The Jan Suraaj Party (JSP), led by Prashant Kishor, is contesting all eight seats. The party revised its candidate list after its initial announcement, replacing Bhushan Jha with Shyam Nandan Yadav in Tirhut Teachers and Ravindra Yadav with Mohammad Imtiyaz (Noorani) in Darbhanga Graduates.(With PTI inputs)

New Delhi: Following confirmation by ITBP of the continuing India-China military stand-off on the Arunachal Pradesh border, India once again cautioned China that maintaining peace and tranquillity in the border areas was essential for the overall development of bilateral ties, echoing PM Narendra Modi’s message to Chinese President Xi Jinping during their meeting last month.The ministry of external affairs (MEA) on Friday did not go into the specifics of the latest face-off, choosing to refer the issue to the defence ministry, but said Chinese divergence from established patrolling patterns created disturbances at the border from time to time.“As we have noted in the past, the situation in India-China border areas gets disturbed from time to time when Chinese forces diverge from established patrolling patterns,” ministry spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal said, adding that the two sides had also agreed to discuss ways to improve understanding of the Line of Actual Control in appropriate areas for better border management.The official said both sides continued to use existing diplomatic and military mechanisms to resolve outstanding issues and avoid misunderstanding and miscalculation along the Line of Actual Control.ITBP DG Shatrujeet Kapur had on Thursday publicly said that Indian and Chinese troops had lately been locked in face-offs at select points along the LAC in Arunachal Pradesh, which “are still continuing”. He, however, added that the ‘Shaurya’ commandos of his force, deployed along the LAC, had done an “excellent job” in dealing with the face-offs.The ITBP chief said India was focusing on building its drone and anti-drone capabilities as “conventional” military resources and infrastructure were not enough to take on the People’s Liberation Army which had undergone a massive capacity upgrade and modernisation, making China a “very strong adversary”.“Drones can pose a challenge as well as present an advantage,” Kapur said, citing the example of Ukraine and Iran which, despite being small nations and with much smaller or no conventional armed forces, had taken on superpowers like Russia and the US respectively.DG Shatrujeet Kapur said ITBP had included drone platoons for all its border units, with 70% of the Rs 400 crore allocated by MHA for modernisation of the force earmarked for upgrading drone warfare capabilities. The force is raising more ‘Shaurya’ commando platoons trained in mountain warfare, new-generation weapons and unarmed combat.Kapur said ITBP must redefine itself as a high-altitude fighting force, distinct from the Army or any other central paramilitary force.Reports of border friction coincide with the ongoing efforts to normalise Sino-India ties that have seen considerable progress since Modi’s meeting with Xi in Russia’s Kazan in 2024.In the meeting last month, Modi underlined the need for both sides to observe existing agreements and understandings on border-related issues. NEW DELHI: After election commissioners S S Sandhu and Vivek Joshi wrote to cabinet secretary TV Somanathan in July objecting to the revised allocation of work among senior commission officers by senior deputy Election Commissioner (DEC) Maneesh Garg without EC approval, the secretariat merely sent them an acknowledgement with a copy to CEC Gyanesh Kumar for information, an RTI reply has revealed.The senior officers among whom the work was reallocated by Garg, who was only filling in for DEC (administration) Bhanu Prakash Yeturu while he was on leave, included Seema Khanna, who was brought in as head of the IT division of EC. Sandhu and Joshi, according to a report in Indian Express dated Sept 23, had in internal notes to DEC concerned, alleged that the ECINET software conceived and managed by the IT division, was too centralised, blocking access to field officers who were authorised by law to make changes to the electoral roll.Explaining the rationale behind the reluctance to take any action, a confidential note on the file shared by the Cabinet secretariat with transparency activist, Commodore Lokesh K Batra (Retd), as part of its 21-page RTI reply, stated that EC being a Constitutional body is insulated from the Executive's interference by design."The...communications are from the ECs in their individual capacity and, while they must be taken with due seriousness, they cannot be seen as a formal communication from the commission as a whole," it said adding that Garg is an officer of the EC and his work and conduct is to be regulated by rules and guidelines of EC."In the absence of any official communication from the commission as a whole, any action at this stage may be inappropriate. It may also be construed as interference in the functioning of the constitutional body," the note underlines before announcing the decision to merely send an acknowledgement to the two ECs, with copies marked to the CEC and the DoPT.Commodore Batra had on September 24 sought copies of the Commissioners' communications, details of the steps taken by the Cabinet Secretariat and the relevant file notings. This was a day after The Indian Express reported that two election commissioners had objected on record 14 times in 10 months to steps involving the addition of new voters and deletion of names from electoral rolls, and had approached the Cabinet Secretary over concerns about the integrity of the voter database.According to the documents shared as part of the RTI response, the two ECs Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi, wrote separate but near-identical letters to Cabinet Secretary TV Somanathan on July 29, 2026, objecting to the conduct of a Garg and an order he issued revising the allocation of work among senior officers. The two Commissioners alleged that the changes were made without prior discussion with the Commission or the officers concerned.A cabinet secretariat file noting dated Aug 3 says that both the ECs have stated that Garg, after assuming the charge as link officer of DEC (Administration), has issued an order regarding work allocation of equivalent and senior officers to him without discussing the revised work allocation with the Commission or the officers concerned.“Further, the ECs stated that this has happened despite repeated oral and written instructions to all concerned officers against taking such actions without prior discussion/approval of the Commission,” noting highlights.“In this connection, we may request the CEC for his opinion on the issue," it said.In another noting dated Aug 4, it is stated that the EC is a “Constitutional body and is insulated from executive interference by design to ensure that it functions independently and in a transparent manner. The working and functioning of the Commission are governed by the rules and guidelines of the Election Commission.”It further states that since the communications are from the ECs in their individual capacity and, while they must be taken with due seriousness, they cannot be seen as a formal communication from the Commission as a whole.The noting also stated that although Maneesh Garg had been appointed by the ACC, he was now an officer of the ECI and his work and conduct is to be regulated and monitored by the rules and guidelines of ECI. It further stated that the ECs have sent these communications for appropriate action; however, in the absence of any official communication from the Commission as a whole, any action at this stage may be inappropriate. It may also be construed as interference in the functioning of the Constitutional Body. "Hence, it would be appropriate to send acknowledgement to both Election Commissioners with a copy to PPS to CEC for information of CEC," it stated.A copy was also marked to be sent to the secretary, department of personnel and training since Garg was an All-India Service officer.

Article Title: Centre bans reuse of single-use medical devices across hospitals; flags recycling of disposables
Article Text:
Govt Flags Recycling Of Disposables In Critical Ops (Generative image)

NEW DELHI: The Centre has directed public and private healthcare facilities across the country to strictly stop reusing medical devices and disposable surgical items meant for one-time use, flagging patient safety risks from the practice, particularly in critical care.In a letter dated Oct 16, the Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS) said it had come to its notice that some private and corporate hospitals were reusing single-use devices after sterilising them, including items used in cardiology, nephrology, oncology, cardiothoracic and vascular surgery (CTVS), neurosurgery and other clinical services.The DGHS said that reuse could expose patients to cross-infection, device malfunction, reduced performance and other complications. It said the practice could violate provisions of the Drugs and Cosmetics Act, 1940, the Medical Devices Rules, 2017, the Clinical Establishments Act, 2010, and applicable infection-control and biomedical waste management requirements.The directive calls on state health authorities and drug controllers to maintain strict vigilance, inspect and monitor healthcare establishments, and take action against violations under applicable laws and regulations.Devices labelled for single use must be used in accordance with the instructions and recommendations of the original equipment manufacturer.The letter, addressed to health authorities in states and Union Territories, the Drugs Controller General of India (DCGI) and the central govt health scheme (CGHS), also flagged cases in which patients were charged the full cost of devices that had been reused, or the cost was reimbursed by govt authorities.The DGHS said the CGHS had issued an office memorandum on the issue in Nov 2016 for hospitals empanelled under the scheme.Single-use devices reportedly reused in India include cardiac catheters and guidewires used in angiography and angioplasty, dialysis equipment, certain surgical instruments and disposable syringes and needles. Such practices raise concerns about infection risks and patient safety, particularly when patients are not informed.Welcoming the directive, the Association of Indian Medical Device Industry (AiMeD) said reuse of devices designed and validated for one-time use could put patients at risk. Its forum coordinator, Rajiv Nath, said enforcement should also clarify responsibility when a device is reused contrary to the manufacturer’s instructions.AiMeD called for regular inspections, traceable records of device use and disposal, staff training and action against violations. It also urged govt to ensure that cost does not become a reason for hospitals to reuse disposable devices.The directive places the responsibility for enforcement on state and UT authorities. However, the letter does not specify a new inspection schedule or a separate penalty for hospitals found reusing such devices.
Article Summary: The Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS) said it had come to its notice that some private and corporate hospitals were reusing single-use devices after sterilising them. The DGHS said that reuse could expose patients to cross- infection, device malfunction, reduced performance and other complications.

Article Title: Northwest India turned drier, south wetter over 70 years, finds IMD study
Article Text:

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: A new IMD study finds that northwest India has turned drier, with its dry climate zone expanding from about a quarter to one-third of the total geographical area, whereas the south peninsula became wetter due to a rise in overall quantitative rainfall over the past seven decades.The findings, published in the IMD’s peer-reviewed journal Mausam, note that the dry zone that once ended in western UP is now extending into the east of the state, with the scientists warning the change could affect paddy cultivation in the north.In northwest India, the hot semi-arid zone grew from about a quarter of the region’s area in 1951-1980 to a third in 1991-2020, while the temperate zone shrank from about a quarter to less than a fifth, meaning that an area equal to roughly 7% of the region moved into the drier zone as temperatures rose and rainfall declined, said the study.It said peninsular India, on the other hand, reported shrinking of its hot semi-arid zone from about 30% of the region to 16%, and most of that land moved into the tropical savannah zone, which now covers three-quarters of the peninsula, a change the authors attribute to rising rainfall over southern India.“Within these broader shifts, Marathwada and west Vidarbha in Maharashtra moved into the hot semi-arid zone, and the tropical monsoon zone extended along the Konkan coast, coastal Karnataka and Kerala,” said the study, conducted by scientists from IMD and Indian Institute of Tropical Meteorology.“When we compared India’s climate map decade by decade from 1951 to 2020, the clearest change was in the north, where the hot, dry zone has pushed east into Uttar Pradesh, and because this is one of the country’s most important farming regions, the timing of sowing and harvesting there needs to be watched closely,” said Ananya Karmakar, the study’s lead author.Since the scientists highlight potential implications for agriculture and the need to track long-term climate shifts, the study could be handy for farm sector policymakers.
Article Summary: A new IMD study finds that northwest India has turned drier, with its dry climate zone expanding from about a quarter to one-third of the total geographical area. The south peninsula became wetter due to a rise in overall quantitative rainfall over the past seven decades. The study could be handy for farm sector policymakers.

Article Title: UP polls: Congress shares initial list with SP, seeks 175-200 seats

NEW DELHI: The Congress has formally begun seat-sharing negotiations with the Samajwadi Party (SP) in poll-bound Uttar Pradesh, submitting an initial list of more than 175 assembly constituencies to the Akhilesh Yadav-led party.Rajendra Pal Gautam, the Congress’ in-charge for Uttar Pradesh, told PTI that the list was shared with SP leaders around two days ago. He added that leaders from both parties would soon hold detailed discussions on the nature of a seat-sharing arrangement.“I can't give you the exact numbers, but we have submitted a list for 175 to 200 seats. The leadership of both parties will sit together to thrash out the nitty-gritties of the seat-sharing arrangement," Gautam said.The Congress has reportedly classified constituencies based on an assessment of its electoral prospects, and seat-sharing negotiations are expected to centre on this assessment.However, several SP leaders remain unconvinced that the Congress has enough political clout to demand 175-200 seats, despite their successful alliance in Uttar Pradesh during the 2024 Lok Sabha elections.The scepticism stems from the Congress’ declining electoral fortunes in Uttar Pradesh since 1989, when it last held power in the country’s most populous state.“I think our party leader Akhilesh Yadav has made it clear that winnability is the sole criterion (for contesting the polls). Anyone can demand anything, but in politics, to reach an acceptable and meaningful solution, you have to move beyond posturing,” a senior SP leader told PTI.The Congress contested the 2022 Uttar Pradesh assembly elections independently but managed to win just two constituencies, down from seven in 2017, when it fought in alliance with the SP. That year, the SP lost power after a single term, securing only 47 seats, while the BJP won a landslide 312 seats in the 403-member ssembly.In 2022, the BJP retained power with 255 seats, while the SP won 111 constituencies.However, the 2024 Lok Sabha elections offered the Congress renewed hope. The grand old party won six seats in Uttar Pradesh, while the SP secured 37 of the state’s 80 seats, limiting the BJP to 33, down from 62 in 2019 and 71 in 2014. The results have strengthened the Congress’ expectations of securing a “respectable share” of seats in the 2027 assembly elections, party leaders acknowledged.“It’s obvious… The 2024 Lok Sabha results were proof that together the two parties can make an impact. Article Title: Study traces how an El Niño changed the pollution map
Article Text:
That atmospheric conditions regulate pollution levels was always known. (File photo)

Study traces how an El Niño changed the pollution map

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

The winter of 2022-23 was remarkably clean in north India with PM2.5 levels down by up to 30% from the average of the previous three years, while peninsular India was considerably dirtier, with average PM2.5 levels in Mumbai spiking by 45%. The next winter (2023-24), the pattern dramatically reversed: PM2.5 spiralled in the North, while falling sharply in peninsular India.What changed within a span of a year? The big difference, as per a new study, was that 2022-23 was a La Niña year, while El Niño prevailed in the subsequent winter.Coming ahead of India’s peak pollution season, the paper, titled ‘Air quality in flux: The baffling ENSO transition in India’, published in Atmospheric Pollution Research journal Thursday, found that La Niña/El Niño conditions altered atmospheric circulation, PM2.5 transport pathways and weather conditions that determine whether pollution disperses or gets trapped.That atmospheric conditions regulate pollution levels was always known. What the study shows is how the atmosphere in winters can behave very differently under El Nino and La Nina conditions, determining where pollutants accumulate and where they are carried away even when emissions remain broadly similar. However, the researchers caution that the study does not establish that El Niño invariably worsens air quality in Delhi or north India.“We are not implying that the 2023-24 El Niño pattern will be repeated this winter. The two years that we studied were unusual and unique,” said atmospheric scientist Gufran Beig, one of the study’s authors. “This year’s El Niño is likely to be the strongest on record.”The study found that during the La Niña winter of 2022-23, stronger winds over north India helped disperse emissions from stubble-burning and local sources. The altered circulation bypassed Delhi and its surroundings and transported these pollutants southwards towards peninsular India. This resulted in substantially higher PM2.5 levels in cities such as Mumbai and Thiruvananthapuram.The following winter, the atmospheric setup changed. Under El Niño, winds over northern India were weaker and passed through areas, including Delhi and Jaipur, rather than carrying pollutants away. The resulting stagnation favoured the accumulation of PM2.5. Jaipur, for instance, recorded an increase of about 50% compared with the 2019-22 average, while Delhi logged a spike of over 10%.Weather conditions also mattered differently in the two years. Rain can remove pollutants from air, while high pressure, weak winds and a shallow boundary layer can trap them close to the ground. In Jaipur, rainfall was more strongly associated with lower PM2.5 during 2022-23, whereas surface pressure became a more important factor during 2023-24, leading to pollution spikes after rain.The researchers also used backward air-mass trajectories to trace where the air reaching cities had travelled from. Jaipur continued to receive air from polluted northern regions during the El Niño winter. Hyderabad, by contrast, received more marine and southern air, helping explain why its pollution pattern moved in the opposite direction.Overall, the study found substantial year-to-year PM2.5 variations from average levels in 2019-22 — ranging from about a 40% decline to a 70% increase, despite no major changes in emissions or pollution-control policies during the period. The authors underlined that the correlations neither establish direct causation nor can these be extrapolated to other years.For Delhi-NCR, this has an important implication: relatively low local or agricultural emissions do not automatically guarantee cleaner air if large-scale circulation turns stagnant. Conversely, even substantial emissions can have a smaller local impact when strong winds efficiently disperse or divert them.The winter pollution story may begin in Delhi and its neighbourhood, but increasingly, the weather that decides its intensity is being written on a much larger canvas.
Article Summary: Study traces how an El Niño changed the pollution map in India. The winter of 2022-23 was remarkably clean in north India with PM2.5 levels down by up to 30% from the average of the previous three years. The next winter (2023-24), the pattern dramatically reversed: PM 2.5 spiralled in the North, while falling sharply in peninsular India.

Article Title: New car safety rules: Rear-crash tests from 2029 to prevent fire, immobilisers from 2027

NEW DELHI: Aiming to prevent fires caused by rear-end collisions, all new cars manufactured from April 2029 will have to comply with a crash-test standard that ensures no fuel spillage or damage to the battery in petrol/diesel and electric vehicles, respectively. The road transport ministry has made compliance with this automotive industry standard mandatory.“To meet the norm, cars will have to be designed and manufactured in a way that prevents damage to the fuel tank or battery in a rear-end collision,” an official said.The ministry has also set mandatory timelines for automakers to comply with other Automotive Industry Standards (AIS), covering occupant protection in offset frontal and lateral collisions, protection of pedestrians and other vulnerable road users, and fitment of immobilisers. The requirements will come into effect from April 2027 onwards.In a notification, the ministry has also made AIS-192 mandatory for Event Data Recorders (EDRs) installed in cars from October 2029. EDRs remain optional but record crash-related data to help establish what happened immediately before and during a collision. Their function is similar to that of an aircraft’s flight-data recorder, or black box.“The rollout will be phased, as the data can help assess driving behaviour and identify corrective measures to prevent future crashes,” the official said.He added that mandatory fitment of immobilisers in cars from October 2027 would be crucial to preventing vehicle theft. An immobiliser is an electronic anti-theft device that prevents an engine from starting unless it detects the correct key or an authorised electronic signal.
Article Summary: All new cars manufactured from April 2029 will have to comply with a crash-test standard that ensures no fuel spillage or damage to the battery in petrol/diesel and electric vehicles. The road transport ministry has made compliance with this automotive industry standard mandatory. The ministry has also made AIS-192 mandatory for Event Data Recorders (EDRs) installed in cars from October 2029.

NEW DELHI: A parliamentary panel has called for “intercensal surveys” -- surveys between two successive censuses -- in India considering that cities and urban settlements undergo major changes in 10 years, and has also recommended review of the criteria for notifying “census towns” to make it more gender inclusive.At present, to qualify an urban area to be a census town, 75% male main working population must engage in non-agricultural activities. As per Census Commissioner of India, the proportion of female workers engaged in non-agricultural activities is not used as a criteria for classifying ‘census towns’ because female workforce participation fluctuates significantly due to social factors, under-reporting, and the informal nature of the work.The parliamentary standing committee on housing and urban affairs has recommended that this criteria is “based on a male-centric understanding of work and does not adequately reflect the growing participation of women in economic activities”. The panel added, “It also fails to capture the contribution of women engaged in self-employment, informal work, home-based work, service sector activities and other forms of employment that are often undercounted.It has highlighted how female labour force participation has been steadily increasing and labour force participation rate for persons aged 15 years and above stood at 34.8% in Aug, 2026. “In this context, continuing with a criterion based exclusively on male main workers would not reflect the changing socio-economic realities of India,” the panel said.The panel, in its report, has referred to a ministry’s suggestion for introduction of periodic intercensal surveys to capture rapid changes in urbanisation and emerging settlement patterns, as well as to address data gaps in the targeting, implementation and monitoring of various schemes and programmes.It has recommended the ministry, in consultation with the Office of Registrar General and Census Commissioner of India (ORGI) and other ministries and departments concerned to examine the feasibility of instituting periodic intercensal surveys for capturing changes in urbanisation, emerging settlement patterns and other relevant urban indicators.ORGI had informed the panel that its primary mandate is to conduct the census and discharge related statutory functions while adding that proposal for conducting periodic intercensal surveys to capture rapid urban changes is a policy matter which may be examined separately by govt.The committee has also recommended the ministry to engage with states and UTs after the release of Census 2027 data to examine the feasibility of converting eligible census towns into statutory urban local bodies, while maintaining an updated database of their status.
Article Summary: At present, to qualify an urban area to be a census town, 75% male main working population must engage in non-agricultural activities. The parliamentary standing committee on housing and urban affairs has recommended that this criteria is ‘based on a male-centric understanding of work’

Article Title: Gurjar Mahasabha flags lack of political representation, seeks greater share in legislatures, institutions

NEW DELHI: The Akhil Bharatiya Gurjar Mahasabha has raised concerns over what it describes as inadequate political and institutional representation of the Gurjar community, claiming that the community has only 20 MLAs among approximately 4,600 legislators in the country and no representation in the Union Cabinet.The organisation said the issue of representation would be a key focus of its national convention at Delhi’s Talkatora Stadium on October 27, where it plans to discuss political participation, reservation-related demands, youth development and social reform.Addressing a press conference at the Press Club of India on Friday, Mahasabha national president Harish Chandra Bhati called for greater representation of the community in political and institutional decision-making, including legislatures, the Supreme Court and the media.Bhati said the community’s contribution to the freedom struggle had not received adequate recognition and called for measures to address the historical and social consequences of the British-era Criminal Tribes Act. He said the law had branded members of the Gurjar community as criminals, contributing to displacement and long-term social exclusion.The representation figures cited by Bhati were claims made by the organisation and were not independently verified.Bhati said political support should be linked to the community receiving an appropriate share in decision-making. He indicated that the Mahasabha would discuss whether the community should reconsider its approach to supporting political parties without adequate representation.The convention will also consider a proposal to establish a separate political platform for the community. Bhati said the organisation would decide its future course after discussions at the gathering, for which it has estimated a turnout of around one lakh people.He also said the Mahasabha would raise the demand for a Gurjar Regiment in the armed forces, arguing that the community’s contribution to the country should receive greater recognition.The organisation said it would pursue its demands through democratic and constitutional means.The Mahasabha also called for the implementation of recommendations made by the Idate Commission, a revision of the base year for the caste census and the inclusion of Most Backward Classes (MBC) reservation provisions in the Ninth Schedule of the Constitution.It further sought the withdrawal of cases related to Gurjar reservation that, according to the organisation, had remained pending for nearly 20 years.National organisation secretary Dr Roop Singh called for the identification and protection of historical sites associated with Gurjar-Pratihar-era rulers. He urged the Archaeological Survey of India to ensure their preservation and called for identification and information boards to be reinstalled at the sites.The October 27 convention will also discuss education, skill development, employment and greater participation of young people in public service.National vice-president Savinder Singh Bhati said the Mahasabha was running an initiative to encourage young people to express their views through peaceful, democratic and constitutional means, while discouraging violence and damage to public property. He also called for guidance and support for young people preparing for competitive examinations, including the IAS and IPS examinations.Another national vice-president, K P Singh Kasana, called for greater awareness about substance abuse and more opportunities for young people through skill development, employment guidance and links with industry.The organisation also plans to adopt resolutions against dowry demands and extravagant wedding spending, as well as costly post-death feasts that it says place financial pressure on families.The convention, being held to mark the 151st birth anniversary of Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel, is expected to bring together community representatives from different states to discuss political representation, social reform and the future direction of the organisation.

NEW DELHI: Ending a quarter-century-long game of hide-and-seek, CBI has arrested Satyendra Kumar , a key fugitive wanted in connection with Bihar’s infamous Fodder scam . The suspect had fled to Nepal and was tracked down during a train journey he took upon returning to India, the agency said.Acting on court orders, CBI had undertaken the probe into the multi-crore corruption scam involving the systematic embezzlement of funds from the Animal Husbandry Department in Bihar during the 1990s. High-profile political figures, including former Bihar chief minister Lalu Prasad Yadav, along with several senior bureaucrats and suppliers, have since been convicted in multiple cases related to illegal treasury withdrawals. The agency had filed dozens of FIRs to untangle a nexus of politicians, bureaucrats, suppliers and middlemen who siphoned off public funds through fake invoices for cattle feed, medicines and equipment.Kumar, alleged to be a supplier, had been on the run since 2001, vanishing into the shadows immediately after the agency filed its charge sheet in the case. His persistent failure to face trial prompted the court to issue an arrest warrant and declare him an absconder, cementing his status as one of the scam’s most elusive figures.It was a to a manhunt that spanned more than two decades across international borders. For over 25 years, Kumar managed to evade the law by taking refuge across the border in Nepal living under an assumed identity. However, the net slowly began to tighten as CBI officials mounted human and technical surveillance to pinpoint his exact movements.The breakthrough came when intelligence revealed that Kumar had re-entered India and was travelling by train from Guna, Madhya Pradesh, to Lucknow, Uttar Pradesh. Acting swiftly on the input, a team was tasked with intercepting the fugitive mid-transit. Units were deployed across Lucknow Railway Station well before the train arrived. Around midnight on Oct 22, the CBI managed to take the accused into custody and placed him under arrest. He was taken to Ranchi on transit remand, where he will finally be produced before the court to face trial.
Article Summary: CBI has arrested Satyendra Kumar, a key fugitive wanted in connection with Bihar’s infamous Fodder scam. The suspect had fled to Nepal and was tracked down during a train journey he took upon returning to India. Kumar, alleged to be a supplier, had been on the run since 2001.

Therefore, I myself have filed a complaint so that the truth comes out. The people should know the truth and also who is behind this,” Siddaramaiah said.He alleged that the video was fabricated and said he had never faced such an incident during his earlier tenures in office.“I was chief minister for 8 years, at that time no incident of blackmailing me happened. Now I have no power,” he said.Siddaramaiah named Kripa Alva, a woman from Dakshina Kannada, and Rakesh Shetty as people who appeared in the video. He claimed that Shetty had admitted to carrying out the operation.“Rakesh Shetty himself has admitted that they did it. There is no truth in this video,” he said.Siddaramaiah said the video first came to his notice on September 26 and denied being worried about the allegations.“After I have not done any wrong, there is no question of me being upset. No matter who sets out to defame me, I know what the truth is. There is no question of me being upset or afraid. This case is 100% created,” he said.Recalling his political career, he said he first became a minister in 1984 and had faced no such incident even when he was chief minister.“Now when I have no power, such a conspiracy is being hatched. It is true that their intention will not succeed,” he asserted.Meanwhile, Karnataka minister Yathindra Siddaramaiah alleged that people from within the Congress were behind the purported sting operation, which he claimed was intended to damage his father's image and blackmail him.Speaking to reporters in Mysuru, Yathindra said the video appeared to show the involvement of a woman from the Congress who wanted a party ticket from Puttur, along with the head of a media organisation.“The whole thing was done to damage my father, tarnish his image, destroy his legacy and blackmail him,” Yathindra said.The minister, who holds the Urban Development portfolio, said the woman's alleged involvement appeared to be linked to her political ambitions.“There is a woman from our party who is involved. As she herself says in the video, she wanted a party ticket from Puttur. Prima facie, it appears that the sting operation was conducted for that purpose,” he said.However, Yathindra cautioned against holding the entire Congress responsible for the alleged actions of an individual party worker.“Just because a party worker has done something like this, it does not mean that our entire party is against us,” he said.
Article Summary: Former Karnataka chief minister Siddaramaiah says he has lodged a police complaint over an alleged “fake sting operation” video targeting him. He alleges that the video was an attempt to blackmail him after he lost power. Karnataka minister Yathindra alleges that people from within the Congress were behind the purported sting operation, which he claimed was intended to damage his father's image.

Article Title: ‘There will be no privatisation’: Haryana CM assures power employees as electricity union calls off strike

NEW DELHI: Haryana’s striking electricity employees on Friday called off their three-day strike following a meeting with chief minister Nayab Singh Saini and power minister Anil Vij.The employees said Saini assured them that private players would not be allowed to enter Haryana’s power sector and that parallel power distribution licences would be revoked. Following the chief minister's assurance, they agreed to restore electricity supply immediately.The next round of talks between the employees’ union and the state government will be held on November 3.The strike, which began on Wednesday night, was being held to protest the Haryana Electricity Regulatory Commission’s (HERC) decision to grant a parallel electricity distribution licence to private company Eleven Power for Gurugram and Nuh.Addressing a joint press conference with Vij and representatives of the electricity employees’ union, Saini emphasised that there would be “no privatisation of any kind."He also pointed out that the HERC is an independent regulatory body.“We have consistently maintained that we stand fully with the electricity employees’ union, and we reiterate that position today. It should be noted that the HERC is an independent agency operating under its own Act.From time to time, we, the state government, are also required to implement its orders and directives,” the chief minister told reporters at a press conference in Panchkula.“Exercising our authority under Section 108 , the government has directed the HERC to review the matter and effectively cancel that provision (private power distribution). The government has provided full assurances. The electricity employees have stated that the strike is being called off, and our employees will now immediately resume their duties. Our position is absolutely firm: there will be no privatisation of any kind,” he added.Thousands of households were left without electricity and water, nearly 1,800 manufacturing units faced disruption, and residents took to the streets as a three-day strike crippled power supply across Gurugram, Haryana’s financial hub, and other cities.Gurugram, which has around 8.5 lakh electricity consumers, witnessed widespread disruptions, particularly in the city’s old areas. According to residents, more than 50,000 households in the area were affected on Thursday, with several localities continuing to face outages after hours of waiting. The agitation also affected Faridabad and Nuh, where residential areas and industrial units reported power cuts.The scale of the disruption was reflected in the complaints received by Dakshin Haryana Bijli Vitran Nigam (DHBVN). An official said the department received more than 3,000 complaints in the first 12 hours of the strike, while DHBVN’s helplines logged around 5,000 outage complaints on Thursday.
Article Summary: Haryana’s striking electricity employees on Friday called off their three-day strike following a meeting with chief minister Nayab Singh Saini and power minister Anil Vij. The strike, which began on Wednesday night, was being held to protest the Haryana Electricity Regulatory Commission's (HERC) decision to grant a parallel electricity distribution licence to private company Eleven Power.

Article Title: Focus on AI & global governance, Brics Parliamentary meet should end with joint statement: Birla
Article Text:

The 12th Brics Parliamentary Forum that India will host on October 26-27 is expected to see high-level participation from member-states like Russia, Iran, China, Brazil and the UAE. Iran will be represented by Speaker Mohammad Baqer Qalibaf.According to Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla, the Forum marks a new chapter in the history of India's parliamentary diplomacy.Talking to reporters on Friday, Birla said the Forum in India would work towards consensus-based dialogue on the critical role of Parliament in strengthening institutions, promotion of human-centred innovation in AI and digital technologies through Parliament, more representative system of global governance and role of Parliament in ensuring a sustainable and inclusive future for Brics countries.The meeting will take place against the continued hostilities in the West Asia region. While that issue is not a part of the official agenda, participants may choose to discuss the conflict on the sidelines. Despite the differences between Iran and the UAE, the Brics summit in India last month had concluded with a unanimous declaration.A meeting of the Secretaries of the delegations will be held on 25 October 2026 to finalise a joint statement for the 12th Brics Parliamentary Forum, according to Birla.The West Asia tensions are unlikely to block the declaration."India's Parliament also holds discussions and engages in dialogue with all countries to build consensus. I hope that, with the agreement of all countries, there will be a joint declaration at the Brics Parliamentary Forum as well," said Birla on Thursday.He said that the Forum would feature bilateral and multilateral interactions with the leaders of visiting delegations and parliamentary friendship groups."The Forum would deliberate on the overarching theme of Strengthening Parliaments for People-Centric Development," he said.According to Birla, a special meeting of the Chairpersons of the International Affairs Committees of of Brics member and partner countries’ Parliament will be held to deliberate on parliamentary diplomacy, capacity building and the exchange of best practices. The conference would also feature a cultural programme.
Article Summary: The 12th Brics Parliamentary Forum that India will host on October 26-27 is expected to see high-level participation from member-states like Russia, Iran, China, Brazil and the UAE. Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla said the Forum marks a new chapter in the history of India's parliamentary diplomacy.

NEW DELHI: Uttarakhand chief minister Pushkar Singh Dhami on Friday spoke with singer Daler Mehndi over the phone, days after a controversy erupted over a cabinet minister reprimanding the singer on stage during an event.According to the CMO, Dhami inquired about Mehndi's well-being and told the artiste that Uttarakhand upholds the rich tradition of 'Atithi Devo Bhava'."Uttarakhand chief minister Pushkar Singh Dhami spoke with singer Daler Mehndi over the phone to inquire about his well-being. During the conversation, the chief minister also discussed the events of the past few days. The chief minister stated that Devbhoomi Uttarakhand upholds the rich tradition of 'Atithi Devo Bhava'," the Uttarakhand chief minister's office said."He emphasised that folk culture, warm hospitality, and a spirit of harmony form the distinct identity of Devbhoomi, where art, culture, and artists have always been welcomed and respected," it added.The controversy erupted after Uttarakhand minister Subodh Uniyal went on stage and expressed displeasure while Mehndi was performing at the Siddhpeeth Maa Kunjapuri Tourism and Development Fair, a cultural event organised by the Uttarakhand government at Narendra Nagar in the New Tehri area on Sunday night.The minister, however, defended his decision to reprimand Mehndi on stage, saying the artiste should not have performed if he was unwell."Daler Mehndi, being a big name, was invited to the Kunjapuri Fair. But during the performance, it became apparent that he was only lip-syncing and not singing. At that point, I thought he was under the influence of some substance. I don't know what, because a medical examination was not conducted," he added.Meanwhile, several people from the entertainment industry, including actor Anupam Kher, stand-up comedian Vir Das and singers Shaan, Palash Sen, Gurdas Maan and Alisha Chinai, came out in support of Mehndi. They said the artiste, who has been singing for three decades, was unwell, did not drink and should have been treated with greater respect."Couple of days ago, I saw a video in which Daler Mehndi ji was singing on stage and some minister got up and spoke to him insultingly. I wasn't there so I don't know but I've known Daler ji for 25 to 30 years. I know that he does not drink and he is one of the finest human beings that I have met. I personally know that he has not been keeping well for two-three years," Kher said in a video on X on Wednesday.

Article Title: 'What happened to Abdul in Telangana?' Congress leader questions Owaisi's 'own leadership' call to Muslims in poll-bound UP

As Asaduddin Owaisi campaigns in poll-bound Uttar Pradesh, urging Muslims to look beyond the Samajwadi Party (SP) and Congress, a Congress leader from Telangana, Owaisi’s home state, on Friday accused the AIMIM chief of advocating a political strategy in UP that he had never implemented in Telangana.Mohammed Waliullah Sameer, Congress in-charge for Owaisi’s Hyderabad Lok Sabha constituency, questioned how many independent Muslim leaders the AIMIM had nurtured beyond its traditional strongholds in Telangana.“Owaisi is telling Muslims in Uttar Pradesh that ‘Abdul’ should no longer spread the carpet for others and should himself become a leader. Fine. But before giving this advice in Azamgarh or Rampur, he should tell us what happened to Abdul in Telangana. Why was he never allowed to move beyond a few selected constituencies?” PTI quoted Sameer as saying.“Muslims certainly need more representation. They need more MLAs, MPs, ministers, mayors, councillors and party office-bearers. But the real question is whether Owaisi has expanded that representation or simply monopolised it in a limited geography,” he added.Sameer pointed out that the All India Majlis-e-Ittehadul Muslimeen (AIMIM) contested only nine of Telangana’s 119 Assembly constituencies in the 2023 elections, accusing the party of supporting the Bharat Rashtra Samithi (BRS) in the remaining 110 seats.“If Owaisi genuinely believed that Muslim youth were being denied platforms by larger parties, why did AIMIM itself leave 110 assembly constituencies ‘untouched’ in the 2023 polls, and were there no capable Muslim lawyers, doctors, entrepreneurs, social workers, women or educated youngsters in those constituencies?” the Congress leader questioned.“AIMIM had, in fact, supported the BRS in most of the constituencies where it did not field candidates. Owaisi was telling Muslims in Uttar Pradesh to stop depending on others, but in Telangana he had voluntarily handed over political space to another party,” he added.Taking a swipe at Owaisi, Sameer said Hyderabad should have become the “strongest advertisement for Owaisi’s political model” if the AIMIM chief’s claims were “genuine”."AIMIM has elected representatives in the municipal corporation and the Hyderabad Lok Sabha constituency. If that model had truly transformed Muslim political power, Hyderabad should today be producing dozens of leaders Instead, political influence has remained concentrated, while most ordinary Muslims continue to struggle with issues related to education, employment, housing, healthcare and civic infrastructure," he stated.The Uttar Pradesh assembly elections are scheduled to be held in February-March 2027, with the Congress expected to contest in alliance with the SP, its current ally.
Article Summary: Asaduddin Owaisi campaigns in poll-bound Uttar Pradesh, urging Muslims to look beyond the Samajwadi Party (SP) and Congress. Congress leader from Telangana accuses AIMIM chief of advocating a political strategy in UP that he had never implemented in TelangANA.

NEW DELHI: Maharashtra Navnirman Sena (MNS) chief Raj Thackeray on Friday accused the BJP of "murdering" democracy by allegedly exerting pressure on the media and using religious polarisation to divert public attention. The barb came after an audio clip triggered a political row over claims of a Rs 500 crore payment to Maratha quota activist Manoj Jarange.In a post on X, Thackeray said the 29-minute recording, which has gone viral in Maharashtra, allegedly featured BJP office-bearers, a senior Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh (RSS) functionary and social media influencers discussing political strategies, media pressure and ways to divert attention from sensitive issues by fuelling religious polarisation.“The chief minister has tried to buy time by saying he’s called for a forensic report on the audio clip, making a show of justice,” Thackeray said, referring to Maharashtra chief minister Devendra Fadnavis 's announcement of a forensic examination.“But if you actually listen to the conversation in this, you’ll realize it’s nothing short of a murder and rape of democracy itself!” he added.Thackeray said the alleged Rs 500 crore payment mentioned in the recording required an explanation but argued that the broader allegations about attempts to influence the media and public discourse also deserved scrutiny. He urged Fadnavis to investigate the conversations allegedly captured in the clip, rather than limiting the inquiry to verifying the recording's authenticity.The controversy erupted after Jarange released a portion of the recording on Thursday, alleging a conspiracy to silence him and weaken his agitation for Maratha reservation. In one segment, a woman allegedly claims that Rs 500 crore had been delivered to Jarange through Shiv Sena MP Shrikant Shinde, son of deputy chief minister Eknath Shinde.The recording also purportedly contains discussions about Jarange's growing political influence ahead of the 2024 Maharashtra assembly elections and strategies to counter his agitation in the Marathwada region.Fadnavis has said the audio clips and conversations would undergo a thorough forensic examination. Shiv Sena leaders have also sought an investigation, while BJP leaders have questioned the recording's authenticity and the timing of its release. BJP IT minister Ashish Shelar called for an inquiry into how the clip was leaked and reached Jarange, while party spokesperson Navnath Ban suggested it could be AI-generated.
Article Summary: MNS chief Raj Thackeray accused the BJP of "murdering" democracy. The barb came after an audio clip triggered a political row over claims of a Rs 500 crore payment to Maratha quota activist Manoj Jarange. He urged Fadnavis to investigate the conversations allegedly captured in the clip.
